title: Understanding Pre-Market Trading: Risks and Opportunities
summary: Learn what pre-market trading is, when it happens, why prices move before the open, the key risks involved, and strategies for navigating extended hours.
body_text: Key time windows The earliest window from 4:00 to 7:00 a.m. ET is dominated by institutional traders and market makers. Spreads are widest and volume is thinnest during this period. The later window from 7:00 to 9:30 a.m. ET sees increasing participation as major economic releases occur and retail platforms come online. How it connects to the regular session Pre-market prices feed into the opening auction that determines the official opening price at 9:30 a.m. ET. A stock trading sharply higher pre-market will likely open above the previous close, though the opening price can differ from the last pre-market trade as the full order book comes together. Why Prices Move Pre-Market Pre-market price movements are driven by information that arrives outside regular hours. Earnings reports are the most common catalyst. Many companies release quarterly results before the open, and a stock can move 5% to 10% or more on earnings surprises before most investors place their first order. Economic data releases create broad market moves. Employment reports, inflation data, and Federal Reserve communications often arrive before 9:30 a.m. ET, pushing index futures and individual stocks. These macro signals affect everything from growth stocks to interest-rate-sensitive sectors. Global market developments drive overnight sentiment. European and Asian market performance, geopolitical events, and commodity price changes all influence how US stocks open. Risks of Pre-Market Trading Pre-market trading carries meaningfully higher risk than regular session activity, and these risks compound for less experienced participants. Low liquidity and wide spreads With fewer buyers and sellers, the bid-ask spread widens considerably. A stock with a $0.02 spread during regular hours might show $0.10 or more pre-market, directly eroding returns on every trade. Price volatility and gaps Thin order books allow large orders to move prices disproportionately. A single institutional trade can push a stock several percent, creating volatile conditions that may reverse once regular trading begins. Limit orders only Most brokerages restrict pre-market to limit orders, protecting against extreme fills. This means orders may not execute if the price moves away quickly. Information asymmetry Institutional traders with faster data feeds react to news before retail investors can read the headline. This creates an uneven playing field where early price moves may already reflect professional positioning. Strategies for Pre-Market Pre-market trading is not for everyone, but investors who participate can approach it more effectively with clear risk management guidelines. Monitor, do not chase Watching pre-market price action provides valuable context for regular session decisions. Seeing how a stock reacts to earnings or news before the open helps you plan entries and exits without necessarily trading in the thinner pre-market environment. Use limit orders with discipline Always set a specific price you are willing to pay or accept. Pre-market volatility can tempt reactive decisions, but disciplined limit orders protect against overpaying during temporary spikes. Focus on high-volume catalysts Pre-market trading is most useful around specific events like earnings releases or major economic data. These catalysts generate enough volume to provide reasonable execution quality. Trading pre-market without a clear catalyst increases exposure to thin liquidity risk. Wait for confirmation A stock gapping up 8% pre-market on earnings may continue higher, or it may reverse as the regular session brings broader participation. Waiting for the first 15 to 30 minutes of regular trading to confirm the direction often provides better risk-adjusted entries than chasing the pre-market move. Conclusion Pre-market trading offers early access to price discovery and the ability to react before the opening bell. For investors who understand the after-hours and pre-market landscape, it can be a useful tool for managing event-driven positions. However, lower liquidity, wider spreads, and greater volatility make it a riskier environment than regular trading. Most investors benefit more from observing pre-market activity to inform their regular session decisions than from actively trading during extended hours. FAQ What time does pre-market trading start? Pre-market trading begins around 4:00 a.m. ET, though most retail activity occurs between 7:00 and 9:30 a.m. ET when liquidity improves. Is pre-market trading riskier than regular trading? Yes. Lower volume, wider spreads, and greater price volatility make pre-market trading meaningfully riskier than the regular session. Should beginners trade pre-market? Most beginners benefit more from monitoring pre-market moves to plan regular session trades rather than actively trading in the thinner extended hours environment. Across animation, product design, architecture, and construction, our work has explored how AI can extend creative intent. From MotionMaker, an AI-powered animation tool in Maya, to new ways large language models help preserve design intent in Fusion through intelligent sketch constraints, we’ve been advancing systems that work with designers’ instincts. In AEC, neural CAD approaches that reason directly with 3D objects and architectural systems are opening new possibilities for how buildings and geometry are conceived, including text-driven design workflows that reimagine how ideas move from concept to form. At the same time, our research has centered on sustainability, data, and human experience. We’ve explored how AI can help assess material conditions hidden inside walls to identify reusable building materials, and how greener construction techniques like 3D-printed floor slabs can reduce waste and carbon emissions. By integrating sensor-collected performance data into product design, convening architects and researchers to study well-being in the built environment, and expanding our work in robotics with autonomous assembly from CAD to finished products, we’re connecting insight to action. And we’ve shared these ideas widely – through our publications library, in blog stories, via interactive experiences, and conversations. Check out our video highlighting how Autodesk Research drove the future of AI, helped design and make a sustainable world, unlocked the power of data, and shared our work with customers and industry. title: AI used car pricing that protects margin
summary: Use AI pricing models, margin floors, and aging triggers to move used inventory faster without sacrificing gross profit.
body_text: Used car pricing is a daily decision. Price too high and inventory sits. Price too low and margin evaporates. AI pricing models help dealerships stay competitive while protecting gross by using live market data and sell-through signals. Why Traditional Pricing Falls Short Market prices shift weekly, sometimes daily Manual updates happen too infrequently Local competition is hard to track consistently How AI Pricing Works AI models ingest multiple signals to recommend pricing changes. Local market listings Days-in-stock and aging curve Reconditioning cost Trim-level demand and seasonality The Margin-Protecting Approach 1) Set Profit Floors Define a minimum acceptable margin by segment. Economy vehicles: lower floor, higher velocity Certified pre-owned: higher floor, lower discounting 2) Use Step-Down Triggers AI can recommend gradual price steps rather than large drops. Day 1-15: full market price Day 16-30: 1-2% adjustment Day 31+: larger reductions if needed 3) Highlight Value, Not Just Price AI can generate listing descriptions that emphasize condition, warranty, and unique features. Inventory Health Metrics to Track Days to turn by segment Gross per unit vs. price position Reconditioning cost recovery rate Price-to-market index Implementation Checklist Normalize trim and option data Define margin floors by category Set aging thresholds for price adjustments Monitor gross per unit weekly Common Pitfalls Overreacting to a single competitor price change Ignoring recon costs when discounting Applying one rule to all segments Conclusion AI used car pricing helps dealers move inventory faster while protecting profit. The key is combining market data with your own margin goals and aging strategy so pricing stays competitive and healthy. What operators should measure before making inventory changes Inventory decisions improve when pricing, aging, and demand signals are reviewed together instead of in isolation. Track turn rate, aging distribution, margin by price band, and response rate to price or inventory changes. That gives managers a practical operating view instead of a static spreadsheet snapshot. AI is most useful here when it shortens decision cycles and makes adjustments easier to validate with actual results. How Clearline fits around inventory workflows While Clearline is voice-first, the platform still matters in inventory-driven workflows because faster follow-up and cleaner call handling protect high-intent shoppers once pricing or demand signals create activity. That helps stores convert interest instead of only modeling it. Use inbound call coverage , outbound follow-up automation , and the demo when comparing how communication quality affects turn and margin. Frequently Asked Questions Can AI actually improve inventory decisions? Yes, when it is used to shorten analysis cycles and link demand signals to action. The biggest mistake is treating AI output as strategy without measuring results. What metrics should be reviewed most often? Track aging, turn, gross by pricing band, and response to pricing changes. Those metrics show whether decisions are helping velocity without destroying margin. Why does communication quality still matter here? Because demand only becomes revenue when stores respond quickly to shopper intent. Pricing and follow-up quality need to work together. What is the best AI for car dealerships? The best setup combines operational intelligence with fast, consistent communication once demand is generated. What still requires human judgment in pricing and turn strategy AI can surface patterns faster than a human team, but pricing and turn strategy still require operator judgment. Managers still have to balance gross protection, local competition, OEM realities, and how urgently the store needs to move a unit. The best use of AI is not to remove judgment. It is to give judgment better timing and better information. How to act before aging becomes a forced decision The earlier a dealership responds to weak demand signals, the more options it keeps. Pricing, merchandising, and follow-up adjustments are all easier when the unit still has time on its side. Once aging becomes visible to everyone, the store is usually negotiating from weakness. That is why forecasting should be treated as an early-action tool, not just a reporting tool. What used-car managers should review every week Used inventory decisions age fast. A weekly review should not just look at the oldest units. It should also look at which vehicles are getting shopper attention without converting, which segments are losing pricing competitiveness, and where the follow-up process is too slow to capitalize on demand. That weekly discipline is where better pricing strategy becomes an operating habit instead of a one-time correction. AI can speed up the signal gathering, but the value still comes from acting on it consistently. What better inventory discipline should produce When forecasting and pricing discipline improve, the result should not just be cleaner reporting. The store should see earlier action on aging risk, steadier margin decisions, and a tighter connection between demand signals and actual follow-up quality. That is when inventory strategy becomes a competitive advantage instead of a reaction to stale units. Related reading If you're exploring similar workflows, read AI Demand Forecasting to Improve Inventory Turn and AI Call Intelligence That Recovers Missed Opportunities .

title: Mission Produce® Introduces Display-Ready Lidded Mango Carton to Support Retail Merchandising and Category Growth

body_text: Oxnard, Calif. – Feb. 10, 2026 – Mission Produce, Inc. (NASDAQ: AVO) (“Mission” or “the Company”) a world leader in sourcing, producing, and distributing fresh Hass avocados, today announced the launch of its new 4-kilo Lidded Mango Carton, a consumer-ready packaging solution designed to help retailers streamline merchandising and drive incremental mango sales. “With demand for mangos continuing to build, 1 retailers are looking for solutions that are both operationally efficient and visually compelling,” said Brooke Becker, Senior Vice President of Sales at Mission Produce. “Our new lidded mango carton was developed with the retailer in mind—it arrives display-ready, creates a strong in-store presence, and supports impulse purchases during key promotional windows. The stackable format allows for flexible placement on-shelf or in secondary displays, enabling retailers to quickly build high-impact merchandising destinations. Mission expects the new carton to help retailers capitalize on the mango momentum during holidays, promotional events, and other high-traffic selling periods. Mission is currently packing the cartons with Peruvian Kents and plans to transition to Mexican supply beginning in March. The carton accommodates round mango varieties, including Kent, Keitt, Tommy Atkins, and Haden, across multiple sizes, offering customers consistent supply options throughout the season. Loan Portfolio As a result of executing on our business plan of providing financing for liquidity, or early investment exits, for alternative asset marketplace participants, Ben’s balance sheet is primarily comprised of loans collateralized by a well- diversified alternative asset portfolio that is expected to grow as Ben successfully executes on its core business. Ben’s balance sheet strategy for ExAlt Loan origination is based on an endowment-style portfolio model for the fiduciary financings we make by utilizing our patent-pending computer implemented technologies branded as OptimumAlt. Our OptimumAlt endowment model balance sheet approach guides diversification of our fiduciary financings across seven asset classes of alternative assets, over 11 industry sectors in which alternative asset managers invest, and at least six countrywide exposures and multiple vintages of dates of investment into the private funds and companies. As of December 31, 2025 , Ben’s loan portfolio was supported by a highly diversified alternative asset collateral portfolio providing diversification across approximately 150 private market funds and approximately 430 investments across various asset classes, industry sectors and geographies. A technology-enabled reforestation company using drones, seed science, and services to restore forests at scale following wildfires and other disturbances. A mobile banking services provider. body_text: Yape alcanzó 15.9 millones de usuarios activos mensuales, que equivale al 84% de la PEA, afianzándose como la marca más valorada y reconocida del país. Durante el 4T25, entre BCP y Yape se incluyeron financieramente a 200 mil personas de 6.6 millones desde 2020. Como parte de su estrategia para reforzar la creación de valor fronterizo, Credicorp suscribió un acuerdo para adquirir el 100% de participación de Helm Bank. Lima, 13 de febrero de 2026.- Durante su presentación trimestral ante inversionistas, Credicorp, grupo financiero líder en el Perú con presencia en Colombia, Chile, Bolivia, Panamá y Estados Unidos, dio cuenta de sus resultados del cuarto trimestre del 2025. El holding , conformado por BCP, BCP Bolivia, Mibanco, Mibanco Colombia, Grupo Pacífico, Prima AFP, Credicorp Capital y Krealo, reportó que la utilidad neta atribuible a Credicorp se incrementó en 25.9% respecto del 2024, alcanzando S/6,925.4 millones, lo que se traduce a un ROE de 19.0%. Estos resultados fueron impulsados por las contribuciones de las principales líneas de negocio, como Banca Universal (que incluye a Yape), Seguros y Pensiones, Microfinanzas, y Gestión y Asesoría de Inversiones. Alejandro Pérez-Reyes, CFO de Credicorp, destacó los resultados financieros y el crecimiento a nivel regional. “Este desempeño refleja una ejecución disciplinada en nuestros negocios principales, el impacto de nuestras iniciativas de innovación y la creciente contribución del ecosistema Credicorp. Además, el margen neto de interés ajustado por riesgo alcanzó un sólido 5.3% para el año completo 2025”. En el cuarto trimestre, la economía peruana registró un crecimiento del PBI cercano al 3,0% interanual, por debajo del crecimiento del 3T25. Los sectores primarios se desaceleraron por una caída en el sector pesca, un crecimiento bajo en el sector minero y una menor producción de cobre. La inflación se aceleró marginalmente y cerró el trimestre en 1,5% interanual (frente al 1,4% del 3T25), en el punto medio del rango meta (1%-3%) del banco central. Credicorp proyecta que el PBI crecerá 3.5% en 2026. Adquisiciones Como parte de su estrategia por fortalecer capacidades y potenciar su propuesta de valor, el holding ejecutó iniciativas clave durante 2025. Se completó la adquisición del 100% del joint venture mantenido con Banmédica, demostrando un sólido encaje estratégico y ejecución disciplinada que refuerzan el negocio de seguros. Más recientemente, se anunció un acuerdo para adquirir Helm Bank en EE. UU., reforzando las capacidades transfronterizas mediante un enfoque focalizado. Transformación digital Durante la presentación, el holding destacó que la innovación y la inclusión financiera siguen siendo fundamentales para su estrategia. “Nuestras plataformas digitales continúan escalando y ampliando el acceso a servicios financieros, al tiempo que profundizan el uso y la generación de valor. Iniciativas como Yape demuestran cómo el uso estratégico de datos, la tecnología y una gestión rigurosa del riesgo permiten impulsar un crecimiento sostenible y generar impacto” , afirmó Gianfranco Ferrari, CEO de Credicorp. Prueba de ello es que, en el cuarto trimestre, Yape alcanzó 15.9 millones de usuarios activos mensuales, que equivale al 84% de la PEA, afianzándose como la marca más valorada y reconocida del país. Otro punto clave es la frecuencia de uso, que alcanzó un promedio de 66 transacciones mensuales por usuario activo (+30.4% interanual). Además, al cierre de 2025, más de 4.1 millones de personas accedieron a un crédito desembolsado a través de la super app. Impacto Sostenible En lo que respecta al despliegue de la Estrategia de Sostenibilidad 2025–2030, el holding alcanzó hitos relevantes en el periodo reportado. BCP y Yape incluyeron financieramente a 200 mil personas durante el 4T25. Así, desde el 2020, han alcanzado 6.6 millones. De la misma manera, Pacífico Seguros cerró el año con más de 3 millones de clientes protegidos con seguros inclusivos y Pacífico Salud aseguró a más de 504 mil personas con seguros de salud inclusivos durante el 2025. Por su parte, Mibanco Perú lanzó “Mibanco por Whatsapp”, una plataforma que integra inteligencia artificial y acompañamiento humano para ampliar la inclusión financiera. Además, la subsidiaria desembolsó créditos a más de 880 mil clientes de la micro, pequeña y mediana empresa (MIPYMEs), por un monto total de S/16,256 millones al cierre del 4T25. En cuanto a financiamientos sostenibles, BCP desembolsó US$3,440 millones, logrando que representen un tercio de su cartera. A esto se suma la ejecución del primer depósito sostenible realizado por un banco peruano, en colaboración con una empresa minera. Los recursos obtenidos se destinarán a financiar proyectos con impacto socioambiental positivo.
